title: Layouts Using Single Words
slide_intent: Use a short sensory word to focus attention because an immediate verbal cue can guide how viewers interpret an ingredient image.
strategic_value: LEAFY, CRUNCHY and JUICY paired with food illustrations can make Burger King’s freshness message memorable at a glance.
demonstration: Three portrait examples pair uppercase sensory headlines with lettuce, onion and tomato illustrations, a small supporting line and corner logo.
practical_value: Choose the short all-caps exception for an evocative out-of-home message of three words or fewer.

content_islands.name: Short-message guidance
content_islands.spec: Place the sentence-case default and uppercase exception at left.

content_islands.name: Three ingredient posters
content_islands.spec: Align the orange, green and cream examples side by side, each with one sensory word above its illustration.

content_islands.name: Example qualification
content_islands.spec: Keep the legal-review note beneath the examples.

ingredient.name: Short uppercase message
ingredient.role: Concentrate sensory meaning in a quickly read phrase.
ingredient.application: Normally use sentence case; for layouts with three or fewer words, all caps may be used, generally for evocative out-of-home work.
ingredient.scope: Historical 2020 partner guidelines, PDF produced January 2021. Printed examples require BK legal trademark clearance and local legal review before use.

reference_purposes.Expression: Color, hand-drawn ingredients and large sensory words create three distinct but related posters.
reference_purposes.Application: The page demonstrates the uppercase exception in out-of-home-style layouts.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Sentence case is primary; all caps is permitted for layouts with three or fewer words.
